content.text:
Start at https://www.legalpeople.com.au and complete the following task.

I’m trying to figure out where I could realistically apply in Australia as a New Zealand-qualified lawyer with about three years of post-qualification experience, and I want a serious browser-based market sweep rather than a skim of one recruiter site. Please start with Legal People Australia, but then widen naturally to other Australian legal recruiters, major job boards, and public law-firm or in-house careers pages so we’re not missing obvious opportunities. Build me a shortlist of exactly 18 to 24 current roles that are genuinely relevant to someone around 2 to 4 PQE, and only include roles where the listing either explicitly welcomes New Zealand qualification or NZ admission, is silent but otherwise looks plausibly transferable, or clearly states Australian admission is required so that distinction is visible. For each shortlisted role, record the job title, employer or recruiter, city/state, practice area, stated PQE or experience range, whether NZ-qualified or NZ-admitted candidates are explicitly mentioned, whether Australian admission appears mandatory, whether a practising certificate or relocation detail is mentioned, and the application link; if a field is missing, mark it as not shown. Keep the work grounded in public pages only. Open and keep available the strongest evidence tabs for at least 8 representative roles spread across different cities or practice areas so I can sanity-check them later, including a mix of recruiter listings and direct employer pages if available. As you go, compare patterns across the market and separate the shortlist into three buckets: clearly eligible now, likely eligible but needs admission clarification, and probably not viable without current Australian admission. Finish with one organized tracker or memo that includes all 18 to 24 roles plus a concise recommendation on where I should focus first by city and practice area, and leave the finished tracker and the most useful evidence tabs open. I would prefer a CrpytoPad Spreadsheet for this tracker.

Rules:
- You may use search engines and open new tabs. When the task asks you to leave a page open, keep it open in its own tab and say in your final answer which page is in which tab.
- Do NOT use cached/archived copies of pages (e.g. web.archive.org); work from the live sites.
- If a site you need is blocked (bot check, login wall, error), first try to get through it — complete a bot check yourself, retry, or use another route to the same page. If it still cannot be reached, say so explicitly in your answer and do not fill in from memory what you could not read on the page.
- When the task is complete, give your final answer as plain text in your last message.

Our Disputes and Investigations group excels at guiding clients through complex and high stakes commercial disputes, class actions and regulatory matters.

Christiana is an accomplished commercial litigation partner with extensive experience acting on significant and complex proceedings. Dan has recently joined the partnership, bringing significant experience across class actions, regulatory disputes and commercial litigation and further strengthening the breadth and depth of the Melbourne practice.

The team acts on major commercial disputes, significant class actions and regulatory proceedings, often involving complex legal and factual issues, substantial financial and reputational exposure and issues of strategic importance to our clients. The team has also been instrumental in successful actions that have established important legal precedents.

Your work will span complex commercial litigation, class actions and regulatory disputes, giving you exposure to a broad range of challenging matters and the opportunity to develop depth as a litigator.

Depending on the matter, you could be developing case strategy alongside the partners, preparing key evidence, pleadings and submissions, working directly with senior client stakeholders and counsel, managing important workstreams within major proceedings and preparing for and being closely involved in hearings and trials.

You will be challenged and supported to develop. You will work closely with partners who are invested in developing excellent litigators and who will give you greater responsibility as your capability and experience grow.

It is an opportunity to sharpen your technical skills, develop your strategic and commercial judgement and build the experience and confidence to become a trusted adviser to clients facing significant disputes.

You will also have the opportunity to work on and assist with the recently announced Royal Commission, with G+T appointed to represent the Victorian State Government.

About you

You are a talented litigator with approximately three to five years’ post admission experience who enjoys difficult problems, high quality work and being part of the strategy.

To succeed in this role, you will bring:

strong litigation experience, ideally across complex commercial disputes, class actions, regulatory litigation or a combination of these areas

excellent analytical, legal reasoning and drafting skills
the ability to get across complex factual, legal and commercial issues and identify what really matters
sound commercial judgement and an ability to understand the broader objectives of the client
confidence building relationships with clients, counsel and colleagues
the ability to take ownership of matters and manage competing priorities
a collaborative approach and an interest in supporting and developing junior lawyers

You do not need to have worked across every type of dispute or tick every box. We are interested in strong litigators with excellent fundamentals, intellectual curiosity, sound judgement and the ambition to continue developing their practice.

About the Opportunity
  
An outstanding opportunity exists for a New Zealand qualified litigation lawyer to relocate to Melbourne and join a high performing General Insurance practice within a leading Australian national law firm.

This role is particularly suited to a New Zealand lawyer with experience in civil litigation, public liability, personal injury or related insurance matters who is looking to take the next step in their career in Australia.

You will join a nationally recognised insurance practice acting for leading insurers, underwriters and corporate insureds across Australia, with exposure to complex and high value disputes.

This is an opportunity to take the litigation skills you have developed in New Zealand and apply them within a larger and highly sophisticated Australian insurance market.

The Work
  
You will work across a broad General Insurance practice, with a particular focus on:


Public liability and general liability claims
Personal injury litigation
Insurance defence litigation
Professional indemnity disputes
Product liability matters
Property damage and third party claims
Coverage and indemnity advice
The work spans both defence litigation and advisory matters, providing exposure to complex disputes and a sophisticated insurer and corporate client base.

What You Will Do


Run your own litigated files with support from experienced senior lawyers and Partners
Draft liability, coverage and indemnity advice
Manage disputes through litigation, mediation and resolution
Engage directly with insurers and corporate clients
Develop strong client relationships
Work alongside experienced insurance practitioners on complex and high value matters
Contribute to the continued development of the wider practice
What We Are Looking For
3 + years PQE in civil litigation
Experience in insurance, public liability, personal injury, general liability or related litigation is preferred
Strong drafting and legal analysis skills
Experience managing your own files with appropriate autonomy
Confident client facing communication skills
A genuine interest in developing a long term career in the Australian legal market
New Zealand qualified lawyers are strongly encouraged to apply
You do not need to have spent your entire career in insurance. The role would suit a strong civil litigator whose experience is transferable into a General Insurance practice.

# Australian Legal Market Sweep: New Zealand-Qualified Lawyer (~3 PQE)

## Executive Summary & Market Findings

As a New Zealand-qualified lawyer with approximately three years of post-qualification experience (target range 2–4 PQE), the Australian legal market represents one of the most accessible international transitions in the common law world. Under the **Trans-Tasman Mutual Recognition Act 1997 (Cth)** (TTMRA), admission as an Australian legal practitioner in any Australian state (such as New South Wales via LPAB, Victoria via VLAB, or Queensland via Legal Practitioners Admissions Board) is essentially an administrative mutual recognition process rather than an academic requalification hurdle. 

However, how Australian employers treat NZ-qualified candidates at the point of application falls into three distinct practical patterns:
1. **Explicitly Welcomed & Supported**: Leading recruiters (such as Tyler Wren) and major national firms actively run campaigns targeting NZ litigators and transactional lawyers, explicitly encouraging New Zealand-qualified lawyers to apply and frequently offering relocation packages. International groups (e.g., Gadens TMIP) and multinational in-house teams with ANZ remits (e.g., AIG, Munich Re) also treat NZ background as directly applicable.
2. **Silent on Jurisdiction but Highly Transferable**: The majority of private practice listings (e.g., Gilbert + Tobin, mid-tier commercial firms via Legal People and Montgomery Advisory) specify "2–4 years PAE" without demanding prior Australian admission. Substantive commercial litigation, front-end construction (Standards Australia / NZS), banking/finance, energy, and corporate law transfer seamlessly because of shared common-law doctrine. In these roles, firms expect you to apply for local admission via TTMRA between offer signing and your start date.
3. **Strictly Preconditioned on Australian Admission / Current Practising Certificate**: High-volume debt recovery, local corporate boutiques (e.g., Nova Legal in WA), and regulated in-house functions (e.g., DLL Group) often mandate a current, unrestricted Australian practising certificate as a day-one prerequisite. Government bodies (e.g., Commonwealth agencies in Canberra) often require Australian citizenship for security clearance purposes, making them unviable without local status.

---

## Strategic Recommendation: Where to Focus First

### 1. By City
* **First Priority: Melbourne (VIC)**
  * **Why**: Melbourne currently shows the highest recruiter receptivity to New Zealand-qualified lawyers. Specialist agencies like **Tyler Wren** and **Legal People** regularly facilitate Trans-Tasman transitions and have established relationships with mid-tier and national firms that value NZ litigators and property lawyers. The Victorian Legal Admissions Board (VLAB) TTMRA process is well-trodden and predictable.
* **Second Priority: Sydney (NSW)**
  * **Why**: Sydney is Australia's largest transactional market with strong demand in **Banking & Finance, Projects/Infrastructure, and Tech/Media/IP** (e.g., Gadens, Gilbert + Tobin, Montgomery Advisory). For transactional or corporate lawyers, Sydney offers the highest volume of mid-level roles, though competition from UK/overseas returnees is slightly higher.
* **Third Priority: Brisbane (QLD)**
  * **Why**: Brisbane's infrastructure, construction, and energy sectors are booming ahead of the 2032 Olympics. As seen in Montgomery Advisory's active listings, firms are seeking 2–4 PQE front-end construction and employment lawyers, where standard form contracts (AS/NZS) share deep historical roots.
* **Secondary / Specialised: Perth & Canberra**
  * Perth is heavily focused on resources and mining; boutique firms often favor local Western Australian networks. Canberra is predominantly government and administrative law, where non-citizens face security clearance barriers for federal agency work.

### 2. By Practice Area
1. **General Insurance & Civil Litigation**: The lowest friction path. New Zealand civil litigators with 3 years of court, file-management, and negotiation experience are in high demand across national insurance practices (defence and coverage).
2. **Projects, Infrastructure & Front-End Construction**: Commercial construction contracts (FIDIC, AS4000) and infrastructure procurement operate on identical principles across the Tasman.
3. **Banking & Finance / Tech & IP**: Top-tier and national firms (G+T, Gadens) explicitly welcome common-law trained transactional associates into structured finance, cyber, and privacy practices.
4. **In-House ANZ Roles**: Multinationals (AIG, Munich Re, technology companies) running integrated Australia-New Zealand legal teams view NZ qualification as an operational differentiator rather than a barrier.

### 3. Immediate Action Plan
* **Initiate TTMRA Paperwork Early**: Lodge your Trans-Tasman Mutual Recognition application with the relevant state board (e.g., NSW LPAB or Victorian VLAB). Even stating *"Admitted in New Zealand; Australian admission via TTMRA currently in progress"* on your CV immediately shifts applications from Bucket 2 into Bucket 1.
* **Target Specialist Recruiters First**: Reach out directly to Tyler Wren and Legal People, citing their current live listings for Melbourne/Sydney. Recruiters are motivated to bridge the minor administrative gap for an immediate 3 PQE candidate.

Tobin

Gilbert + Tobin is built on enduring values of excellence, trust, respect, integrity and good corporate citizenship. We are a leading firm with over 500 lawyers, trusted by our clients to navigate today’s increasingly complex world.

We are purpose-built for our clients’ most complex work - across transactions, disputes and regulation. Our partners are leaders in their fields, delivering the highest quality of legal advice and providing an exceptional edge for our clients. They also provide our lawyers the opportunity to work with and learn from them. We are innovators in the use of technology, redefining value and service in the legal industry.

Our open, merit-based culture attracts and inspires the best legal talent. Founded in 1988, G+T’s journey has been one of relentless ambition and rapid progress, achieving extraordinary success in just over three decades.

We remain as determined as ever to be the best it’s possible to be

About Disputes and Investigations

Our Disputes and Investigations group excels at guiding clients through complex and high stakes commercial disputes, class actions and regulatory matters.

In Melbourne, you will work directly with Janet Whiting, Christiana McCudden and Dan Moloney on some of the most complex and high profile disputes in the market.

Janet is one of Australia’s pre eminent commercial litigators, renowned for her strategic advice, detailed analysis and ability to secure commercial outcomes. Christiana is an accomplished commercial litigation partner with extensive experience acting on significant and complex proceedings. Dan has recently joined the partnership, bringing significant experience across class actions, regulatory disputes and commercial litigation and further strengthening the breadth and depth of the Melbourne practice.

The team acts on major commercial disputes, significant class actions and regulatory proceedings, often involving complex legal and factual issues, substantial financial and reputational exposure and issues of strategic importance to our clients. The team has also been instrumental in successful actions that have established important legal precedents.

About the opportunity

For a mid level lawyer, this is an opportunity to do more than support on large matters. You will have the opportunity to take ownership of significant aspects of a case, work directly with partners, clients and leading counsel, contribute to litigation strategy and see matters through from the early st
</untrusted_web_content>

args.title: Read G+T requirements section

content.text:
<untrusted_web_content source="repl">
[Context: Sandboxed JavaScript output that may include browser pages, fetched URLs, nested tool results, or remote module data. URLs require status and redirect verification before citation.]
ages of a dispute to hearing.

Your work will span complex commercial litigation, class actions and regulatory disputes, giving you exposure to a broad range of challenging matters and the opportunity to develop depth as a litigator.

Depending on the matter, you could be developing case strategy alongside the partners, preparing key evidence, pleadings and submissions, working directly with senior client stakeholders and counsel, managing important workstreams within major proceedings and preparing for and being closely involved in hearings and trials.

You will be challenged and supported to develop. You will work closely with partners who are invested in developing excellent litigators and who will give you greater responsibility as your capability and experience grow.

It is an opportunity to sharpen your technical skills, develop your strategic and commercial judgement and build the experience and confidence to become a trusted adviser to clients facing significant disputes.

You will also have the opportunity to work on and assist with the recently announced Royal Commission, with G+T appointed to represent the Victorian State Government.

About you

You are a talented litigator with approximately three to five years’ post admission experience who enjoys difficult problems, high quality work and being part of the strategy.

To succeed in this role, you will bring:

strong litigation experience, ideally across complex commercial disputes, class actions, regulatory litigation or a combination of these areas
demonstrated court experience, including preparing pleadings and evidence, briefing counsel and preparing matters for hearing
excellent analytical, legal reasoning and drafting skills
the ability to get across complex factual, legal and commercial issues and identify what really matters
sound commercial judgement and an ability to understand the broader objectives of the client
confidence building relationships with clients, counsel and colleagues
the ability to take ownership of matters and manage competing priorities
a collaborative approach and an interest in supporting and developing junior lawyers

You do not need to have worked across every type of dispute or tick every box. We are interested in strong litigators with excellent fundamentals, intellectual curiosity, sound judgement and the ambition to continue developing their practice.

Why G+T?

Exceptional work. You will work on major commercial disputes, class actions and regulatory matters

About the Opportunity
  
An outstanding opportunity exists for a New Zealand qualified litigation lawyer to relocate to Melbourne and join a high performing General Insurance practice within a leading Australian national law firm.

This role is particularly suited to a New Zealand lawyer with experience in civil litigation, public liability, personal injury or related insurance matters who is looking to take the next step in their career in Australia.

You will join a nationally recognised insurance practice acting for leading insurers, underwriters and corporate insureds across Australia, with exposure to complex and high value disputes.

This is an opportunity to take the litigation skills you have developed in New Zealand and apply them within a larger and highly sophisticated Australian insurance market.

The Work
  
You will work across a broad General Insurance practice, with a particular focus on:


Public liability and general liability claims
Personal injury litigation
Insurance defence litigation
Professional indemnity disputes
Product liability matters
Property damage and third party claims
Coverage and indemnity advice
The work spans both defence litigation and advisory matters, providing exposure to complex disputes and a sophisticated insurer and corporate client base.

What You Will Do


Run your own litigated files with support from experienced senior lawyers and Partners
Draft liability, coverage and indemnity advice
Manage disputes through litigation, mediation and resolution
Engage directly with insurers and corporate clients
Develop strong client relationships
Work alongside experienced insurance practitioners on complex and high value matters
Contribute to the continued development of the wider practice
What We Are Looking For
3 + years PQE in civil litigation
Experience in insurance, public liability, personal injury, general liability or related litigation is preferred
Strong drafting and legal analysis skills
Experience managing your own files with appropriate autonomy
Confident client facing communication skills
A genuine interest in developing a long term career in the Australian legal market
New Zealand qualified lawyers are strongly encouraged to apply
You do not need to have spent your entire career in insurance. The role would suit a strong civil litigator whose experience is transferable into a General Insurance practice.

# Australian Legal Market Sweep: New Zealand-Qualified Lawyer (~3 PQE)

## Executive Summary & Market Findings

As a New Zealand-qualified lawyer with approximately three years of post-qualification experience (target range 2–4 PQE), the Australian legal market represents one of the most accessible international transitions in the common law world. Under the **Trans-Tasman Mutual Recognition Act 1997 (Cth)** (TTMRA), admission as an Australian legal practitioner in any Australian state (such as New South Wales via LPAB, Victoria via VLAB, or Queensland via Legal Practitioners Admissions Board) is essentially an administrative mutual recognition process rather than an academic requalification hurdle. 

However, how Australian employers treat NZ-qualified candidates at the point of application falls into three distinct practical patterns:
1. **Explicitly Welcomed & Supported**: Leading recruiters (such as Tyler Wren) and major national firms actively run campaigns targeting NZ litigators and transactional lawyers, explicitly encouraging New Zealand-qualified lawyers to apply and frequently offering relocation packages. International groups (e.g., Gadens TMIP) and multinational in-house teams with ANZ remits (e.g., AIG, Munich Re) also treat NZ background as directly applicable.
2. **Silent on Jurisdiction but Highly Transferable**: The majority of private practice listings (e.g., Gilbert + Tobin, mid-tier commercial firms via Legal People and Montgomery Advisory) specify "2–4 years PAE" without demanding prior Australian admission. Substantive commercial litigation, front-end construction (Standards Australia / NZS), banking/finance, energy, and corporate law transfer seamlessly because of shared common-law doctrine. In these roles, firms expect you to apply for local admission via TTMRA between offer signing and your start date.
3. **Strictly Preconditioned on Australian Admission / Current Practising Certificate**: High-volume debt recovery, local corporate boutiques (e.g., Nova Legal in WA), and regulated in-house functions (e.g., DLL Group) often mandate a current, unrestricted Australian practising certificate as a day-one prerequisite. Government bodies (e.g., Commonwealth agencies in Canberra) often require Australian citizenship for security clearance purposes, making them unviable without local status.

## Strategic Recommendation: Where to Focus First

### 1. By City
* **First Priority: Melbourne (VIC)**
  * **Why**: Melbourne currently shows the highest recruiter receptivity to New Zealand-qualified lawyers. Specialist agencies like **Tyler Wren** and **Legal People** regularly facilitate Trans-Tasman transitions and have established relationships with mid-tier and national firms that value NZ litigators and property lawyers. The Victorian Legal Admissions Board (VLAB) TTMRA process is well-trodden and predictable.
* **Second Priority: Sydney (NSW)**
  * **Why**: Sydney is Australia's largest transactional market with strong demand in **Banking & Finance, Projects/Infrastructure, and Tech/Media/IP** (e.g., Gadens, Gilbert + Tobin, Montgomery Advisory). For transactional or corporate lawyers, Sydney offers the highest volume of mid-level roles, though competition from UK/overseas returnees is slightly higher.
* **Third Priority: Brisbane (QLD)**
  * **Why**: Brisbane's infrastructure, construction, and energy sectors are booming ahead of the 2032 Olympics. As seen in Montgomery Advisory's active listings, firms are seeking 2–4 PQE front-end construction and employment lawyers, where standard form contracts (AS/NZS) share deep historical roots.
* **Secondary / Specialised: Perth & Canberra**
  * Perth is heavily focused on resources and mining; boutique firms often favor local Western Australian networks. Canberra is predominantly government and administrative law, where non-citizens face security clearance barriers for federal agency work.

### 2. By Practice Area
1. **General Insurance & Civil Litigation**: The lowest friction path. New Zealand civil litigators with 3 years of court, file-management, and negotiation experience are in high demand across national insurance practices (defence and coverage).
2. **Projects, Infrastructure & Front-End Construction**: Commercial construction contracts (FIDIC, AS4000) and infrastructure procurement operate on identical principles across the Tasman.
3. **Banking & Finance / Tech & IP**: Top-tier and national firms (G+T, Gadens) explicitly welcome common-law trained transactional associates into structured finance, cyber, and privacy practices.
4. **In-House ANZ Roles**: Multinationals (AIG, Munich Re, technology companies) running integrated Australia-New Zealand legal teams view NZ qualification as an operational differentiator rather than a barrier.

### 3. Immediate Action Plan
* **Initiate TTMRA Paperwork Early**: Lodge your Trans-Tasman Mutual Recognition application with the relevant state board (e.g., NSW LPAB or Victorian VLAB). Even stating *"Admitted in New Zealand; Australian admission via TTMRA currently in progress"* on your CV immediately shifts applications from Bucket 2 into Bucket 1.
* **Target Specialist Recruiters First**: Reach out directly to Tyler Wren and Legal People, citing their current live listings for Melbourne/Sydney. Recruiters are motivated to bridge the minor administrative gap for an immediate 3 PQE candidate.
